\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Decision from one-sided error]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.decidesInTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.decidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.exists_outputWith_of_outputProb_pos, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every
input $x$, every branch halts within $T(|x|)$ steps, output $1$ has probability at least
$2/3$ when $x\in L$, and every branch outputs $0$ when $x\notin L$. Then every input's
branches halt within that time, and $x\in L$ exactly when some branch of length $T(|x|)$
halts with output exactly $1$.
\end{theorem}

  {Randomized.BPTIME}
  {direct}
  {arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}
  {pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003}
For every time bound $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, every language decidable by a
finite deterministic Turing machine in time at most a constant multiple of $T$ belongs
to the class of languages decidable with bounded error in time at most a constant
multiple of $T$.
\end{theorem}

Every language decidable by a finite deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time is
decidable by a finite randomized Turing machine in polynomial time with acceptance
probability at least $2/3$ on every input and halting on every choice sequence of the
prescribed length.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized time is contained in nondeterministic time]
\lean{Randomized.RTIME_subset_NTIME}
\label{Randomized.RTIME_subset_NTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Randomized.RTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.decidesInTime}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RTIME}(T) \subseteq
\mathrm{NTIME}(T)$. The randomized class requires a finite machine running in time
bounded by a constant multiple of $T$, halting on every branch, accepting members with
probability at least $2/3$, and never accepting nonmembers; the nondeterministic class
requires a finite machine with that time bound, halting on every branch and accepting
exactly the members.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-Sided Randomized Polynomial Time Is in NP]
\lean{Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_NP}
\label{Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.NP_eq_iUnion_NTIME, Randomized.RP_PTM, Randomized.RTIME_subset_NTIME}
\difficulty{3}
Every language decidable in polynomial time by a randomized machine with one-sided error
and acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members belongs to NP: membership can be
certified by a witness of length bounded by a polynomial in the input length, with the
input and witness accepted by a deterministic polynomial-time verifier.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-Sided Randomized Polynomial Time Is in Bounded-Error Polynomial Time]
\lean{Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_BPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_BPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.RP_PTM, Randomized.RTIME_subset_BPTIME}
\difficulty{1}
Every language decidable in polynomial time by a randomized machine with one-sided error
and acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members is decidable in polynomial time by
a randomized machine that outputs the correct membership answer with probability at
least $2/3$ on every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CoRP Is Contained in BPP]
\lean{Randomized.coRP_PTM_subset_BPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.coRP_PTM_subset_BPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_BPP_PTM, Randomized.coRP_PTM, Randomized.compl_mem_BPP_PTM}
\difficulty{3}
Every language whose complement is decidable by a randomized Turing machine in
polynomial time with one-sided error is decidable by a randomized Turing machine in
polynomial time with two-sided error at most $1/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[RP is contained in BPP]
\lean{Randomized.InRP.inBPP}
\label{Randomized.InRP.inBPP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InRP, Randomized.VerifierModel, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_true}
\difficulty{3}
Let $E$ be a verifier model and let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If $L$ has an
$E$-efficient randomized verifier with polynomially bounded randomness, acceptance
probability at least $2/3$ on members, and zero acceptance probability on nonmembers,
then it has an $E$-efficient randomized verifier whose acceptance and rejection
probabilities on members and nonmembers, respectively, are each at least $2/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CoRP implies BPP under complementation]
\lean{Randomized.InCoRP.inBPP}
\label{Randomized.InCoRP.inBPP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ClosedUnderNot, Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InBPP.compl, Randomized.InCoRP, Randomized.InRP.inBPP, Randomized.VerifierModel}
\difficulty{3}
Let $E$ be a verifier model whose efficient verifiers are closed under Boolean negation,
and let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If the complement of $L$ has an $E$-efficient
randomized verifier with polynomially bounded randomness, acceptance probability at
least $2/3$ on members, and rejection probability exactly $1$ on nonmembers, then $L$
has an $E$-efficient randomized verifier with both correctness probabilities at least
$2/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time coRP is contained in BPP]
\lean{Randomized.InCoRP.inBPP_polyTime}
\label{Randomized.InCoRP.inBPP_polyTime}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InCoRP, Randomized.InCoRP.inBPP, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.polyTimeModel_closedUnderNot}
\difficulty{1}
Every language of bit strings that has a polynomial-time randomized verifier with
polynomially bounded randomness, acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members, and
zero acceptance probability on nonmembers also has a polynomial-time randomized verifier
whose acceptance and rejection probabilities on members and nonmembers, respectively,
are each at least $2/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-Sided Randomized Recognition Lies in NP]
\lean{Randomized.mem_NP_of_inRP_polyTimeModel}
\label{Randomized.mem_NP_of_inRP_polyTimeModel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.inter_mem_P, Complexity.lenEq_preimage_mem_P, Complexity.mem_NP_iff_exists_length_le, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary, Randomized.InRP, Randomized.boolVerifier, Randomized.exists_ofFn_eq, Randomized.exists_ofFn_of_randProb_pos, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If a polynomial-time verifier using a polynomial
number of uniformly random bits accepts each member with probability at least $2/3$ and
never accepts a nonmember, then $L$ belongs to $	extsf{NP}$: there are constants
$C,c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a polynomial-time decidable language $V$ such that $x\in L$
exactly when some string $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$ has $x\mathbin{++}u\in V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[BPP equals P when P equals NP]
\lean{Randomized.inBPP_polyTimeModel_iff_mem_P_of_P_eq_NP}
\label{Randomized.inBPP_polyTimeModel_iff_mem_P_of_P_eq_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.PH_eq_P_of_P_eq_NP, Complexity.SigmaP_subset_PH, Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.inBPP_polyTimeModel_of_mem_P, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.sipser_gacs_polyTime}
\difficulty{3}
If $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, then for every language $L$ of bit strings, $L$ belongs
to BPP relative to the polynomial-time verifier model if and only if $L \in \mathrm{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Efficient reduced verifier]
\lean{Randomized.exists_eff_reducedVerifier}
\label{Randomized.exists_eff_reducedVerifier}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.output_length_le, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.preimage_mem_P, Randomized.boolVerifier, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeComputable_sliceTake, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.sliceTake, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable map from bit strings to bit strings. Let $M$ map
pairs of bit strings to a bit, and suppose the verifier returning $M(x,r)$ is efficient
in the specified polynomial-time model. For any natural numbers $a,k$, there are natural
numbers $a',k'$ such that the verifier returning $M(f(x),r')$, where $r'$ is the prefix
of $r$ of length $a(|f(x)|+1)^k$, is efficient in that model, and $a(|f(x)|+1)^k\le
a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$ for every bit string $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Closure under polynomial-time reductions]
\lean{Randomized.InBPP.of_polyTimeReducible}
\label{Randomized.InBPP.of_polyTimeReducible}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ and $L'$ be languages of bit strings. If $L'$ is polynomial-time many-one
reducible to $L$ and $L$ belongs to the bounded-error class defined by the specified
polynomial-time verifier model, then $L'$ belongs to that class as well.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[RP is closed under polynomial-time reductions]
\lean{Randomized.InRP.of_polyTimeReducible}
\label{Randomized.InRP.of_polyTimeReducible}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InRP, Randomized.exists_eff_reducedVerifier, Randomized.exists_ofFn_eq, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.randProb_take}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ and $L'$ be languages of bit strings, and suppose $L'$ is polynomial-time
many-one reducible to $L$. If $L$ has an RP verifier in the polynomial-time verifier
model, then $L'$ also has an RP verifier in that model.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CoRP is closed under polynomial-time reductions]
\lean{Randomized.InCoRP.of_polyTimeReducible}
\label{Randomized.InCoRP.of_polyTimeReducible}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InCoRP, Randomized.InRP.of_polyTimeReducible, Randomized.polyTimeModel}
\difficulty{1}
Let $L$ and $L'$ be languages of bit strings, and suppose $L'$ is polynomial-time
many-one reducible to $L$. If $L$ has a coRP verifier in the polynomial-time verifier
model, then $L'$ also has a coRP verifier in that model.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Collapse of the Polynomial Hierarchy]
\lean{Randomized.PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_inBPP_SAT3}
\label{Randomized.PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_inBPP_SAT3}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.mem_PPoly_iff, Complexity.PH, Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_subset_PPoly, Complexity.SAT3, Complexity.SAT3_NPHard, Complexity.SigmaP, Randomized.InBPP, Randomized.InBPP.of_polyTimeReducible, Randomized.adleman_polyTime, Randomized.polyTimeModel}
\difficulty{1}
If $3$-CNF satisfiability belongs to $\mathrm{BPP}$ as defined using the polynomial-time
verifier model, then the polynomial hierarchy equals its second existential level:
$\mathrm{PH}=\Sigma_2^P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Weak one-sided randomized recognition]
\lean{Randomized.InRPWeak}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b003}
\label{Randomized.InRPWeak}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.boolVerifier, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.randProb}
Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $c$ be a natural number, and let $L$ be a language of
Boolean lists. The property holds when there are a verifier $M$ from pairs of Boolean
lists to Boolean values and natural numbers $a,k$ such that the verifier obtained from
$M$ is efficient according to $E$, and for every Boolean list $x$, both conditions hold:
if $x\in L$, the probability that $M$ accepts a uniformly random Boolean list of length
$\operatorname{polyLen}(a,k,|x|)$ is at least
$\min\!\left(\frac23,\frac{1}{(|x|+1)^c}\right)$; if $x\notin L$, then $M$ rejects every
Boolean list of that length.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Strong one-sided randomized recognition]
\lean{Randomized.InRPStrong}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b003}
\label{Randomized.InRPStrong}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.boolVerifier, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.randProb}
Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $d$ be a natural number, and let $L$ be a language of
Boolean lists. There must exist a Boolean verifier $M$ and natural numbers $a,k$ such
that the verifier induced by $M$ is efficient according to $E$. For every Boolean list
$x$, if $x\in L$, then $M$ accepts a uniformly random string of the prescribed
random-bit length with probability at least $1-\left(\frac12\right)^{(|x|+1)^d+1}$; if
$x\notin L$, then $M$ rejects every string of that length.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Strong randomized recognition implies randomized recognition]
\lean{Randomized.InRPStrong.toInRP}
\label{Randomized.InRPStrong.toInRP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InRP, Randomized.InRPStrong}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, and let $d$ be a
natural number. If there is an efficient verifier with a polynomial random-bit bound
that rejects every nonmember for every choice of random bits and accepts each member $x$
with probability at least $1-(1/2)^{(|x|+1)^d+1}$, then $L$ has an efficient verifier
with a polynomial random-bit bound that accepts every member with probability at least
$2/3$ and rejects every nonmember for every choice of random bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weak randomized recognition from randomized recognition]
\lean{Randomized.InRP.toInRPWeak}
\label{Randomized.InRP.toInRPWeak}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InRP, Randomized.InRPWeak}
\difficulty{1}
Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, and let $c$ be a
natural number. If some verifier runs efficiently, accepts every member of $L$ with
probability at least $2/3$ using a polynomial number of random bits, and rejects every
nonmember for every choice of those bits, then there is an efficient verifier with a
polynomial random-bit bound that accepts each member $x$ with probability at least
$\min\{2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c}\}$ and still rejects every nonmember for every choice of its
random bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Error reduction for randomized languages]
\lean{Randomized.rp_error_reduction}
\label{Randomized.rp_error_reduction}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ClosedUnderAny, Randomized.InRPStrong, Randomized.InRPWeak, Randomized.anyVerifier, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.exists_ofFn_eq, Randomized.one_sub_pow_le_half_pow, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_blockCount, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_le_one, Randomized.randProb_nonneg, Randomized.randProb_not}
\difficulty{7}
Let $E$ be a verifier model that is closed under testing whether any of a polynomial
number of consecutive random blocks is accepted. Suppose a language $L$ has an
$E$-efficient verifier with polynomially many random bits, perfect rejection on inputs
outside $L$, and acceptance probability at least $\min(2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c})$ on each input
$x\in L$, for some natural number $c$. Then, for every natural number $d$, $L$ has an
$E$-efficient verifier with polynomially many random bits, perfect rejection outside
$L$, and acceptance probability at least $1-2^{-((|x|+1)^d+1)}$ on every $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weak and standard one-sided randomized recognition]
\lean{Randomized.inRPWeak_iff_inRP}
\label{Randomized.inRPWeak_iff_inRP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.ClosedUnderAny, Randomized.InRP, Randomized.InRP.toInRPWeak, Randomized.InRPStrong.toInRP, Randomized.InRPWeak, Randomized.rp_error_reduction}
\difficulty{1}
Let $E$ be a verifier model whose efficient verifiers are closed under the specified
disjunction of polynomially many random-tape tests. For every natural number $c$ and
every language $L$, weak one-sided recognition—an efficient verifier with perfect
rejection outside $L$ and acceptance probability at least $\min(2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c})$ on
inputs in $L$—is equivalent to standard one-sided randomized recognition, with
acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on inputs in $L$ and perfect rejection outside
$L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time randomized error reduction]
\lean{Randomized.rp_error_reduction_polyTime}
\label{Randomized.rp_error_reduction_polyTime}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InRPStrong, Randomized.InRPWeak, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.polyTimeModel_closedUnderAny, Randomized.rp_error_reduction}
\difficulty{1}
Suppose a language $L$ has a polynomial-time randomized verifier with polynomially many
random bits, perfect rejection on inputs outside $L$, and acceptance probability at
least $\min(2/3,(|x|+1)^{-c})$ on each input $x\in L$, for some natural number $c$.
Then, for every natural number $d$, it has a polynomial-time randomized verifier with
polynomially many random bits, perfect rejection outside $L$, and acceptance probability
at least $1-2^{-((|x|+1)^d+1)}$ on every $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}
